about: What the maker's user manual says, as a profile: its figures, every command and setting it prints, and each of its procedures in this repository's own words with the page it is on. The manual itself is the maker's and is not kept here; this file cites it. A figure or a command is the manual's own; a step is a summary of it, not its text.

source.title: User Manual, CNC Router 4030-Evo Ultra 2
source.page_numbers: The manual numbers its pages 01 to 35 from the package list, the fifth sheet of the file: a page cited here is the manual's own number, and the sheet of the file is that number plus four. The cover, the welcome, the parameters and the catalog come before page 01 and are cited as sheets.
source.read: 2026-11-10, every sheet, as pictures: the file's text layer is unreadable for most pages (fonts without a character map), so nothing here was taken from it unchecked.
left_out: the download link and its QR code (sheet 2): a shared link is not kept in this repository
the default password of the controller's own WiFi (page 31): a credential is not kept here, and the page is cited for it

applies_to.note: The manual is the 4030's. The two share the controller, the Z axis, the trim router, the probe and the software; the 4060's Y travel is longer. A figure below is the 4030's unless it says otherwise, and what this machine's controller says for itself ($$) is the word to trust for travel.

spindle_dial.note: The trim router's speed is set by the dial on its body, and these are approximate. The controller switches it; it does not set its speed.
cautions: run long at low speed, the motor overloads
the dial turns from 1 to 6 and back and is not forced past either end
the chuck and the body are hot after running
check the tool's path clears the clamps

procedures.name: first cut
steps: release the emergency stop, connect USB, switch on
install the CH340 driver and find the serial port
open Candle, choose the port at 115200 baud
the console shows the Grbl 1.3a banner when connected
press Home: the spindle goes to its home position; if it fails, FAQ Q7
clamp the MDF
choose a step and a feed, and jog the bit down to the stock's surface until a sheet of paper is just gripped under it and can still be pulled through
set the origin there: Zero XY and Zero Z; switch the trim router on at its own switch and choose its speed; Send
finished

procedures.name: Z probe
steps: measure the probe plate's thickness with calipers (19.08 mm in the manual's example)
put the measured thickness in the probe commands in place of the default Z19
clip the lead to the bit and stand the plate on the stock under the bit
Zero XY, then the Z-probe button: the bit goes down until it touches, the touch is given the plate's thickness as its Z, and the bit lifts 5 mm
take the probe off the bit and the stock before cutting

procedures.name: emergency stop
steps: press it down when the machine misbehaves
USB drops, and the control software says it is not connected
turn it clockwise to release it

procedures.name: a limit switch touched
steps: outside the working area the tool touches a red limit switch, the machine stops and its status is Alarm
Unlock, the status goes to Idle, then jog the other way, off the switch

procedures.name: the Macro button
steps: the button on the control box homes the machine as shipped
$User/Macro0= followed by a command, or by commands joined with ampersands, gives it another
$User/Macro0=$SD/Run= followed by a file's name makes it run that file from the memory card

procedures.name: WiFi and the WebUI
steps: powered on, the controller is a WiFi access point of its own; its default password is on page 31
a captive page may open by itself and is cancelled
the WebUI (ESP3D for GRBL ESP32) is at the controller's address in a browser
its controls: a home for each axis and for all, jog rings in steps of 0.1, 1 and 10, a custom button, motors on and off, zero for each axis and for all, feeds for XY and for Z
its GRBL panel: unlock, feed and spindle overrides, spindle, flood (M08) and mist (M07), reset, the memory card's files with upload and send
its probe panel: maximum travel 40 mm, feed 100 mm/min, plate thickness 0.5 mm and retract 5 mm as pictured, and Start probe; the panel is switched on under Preferences when it is not shown
a console for commands; the GRBL configuration and the ESP3D settings, both recommended left alone

assemblies: trim router with ER11 collet and nut

assembly.step: remove the four acrylic blocks fixed to the aluminium profile
gantry: space the nuts in the Y-axis profile with the spacer template tool; raise the gantry on two MDF boards, set its position with the tool, fix it with M6x20 bolts and washers on both sides
Z axis: fix the Z-axis assembly to the gantry with M5x14 bolts, the top row of six loosely first, then the bottom row, set its height with the spacer template tool, then tighten all
trim router holder: two M5x22 bolts, washers and nuts in its opening, left loose; four M6x18 hex bolts and washers hold it to the Z slider, each pressed into its hole by hand before the wrench
trim router: the ER11 1/8 inch collet and nut come fitted; the router goes into the holder from above, and the two M5x22 bolts are tightened
drag chain bracket: two M5x20 button head bolts hold it on the Z-axis assembly
drag chain: one end to the gantry's black profile with two M3x8 bolts and T-nuts, the other to the bracket with two M3x8 bolts
cable clips: M3x8 bolts hold them to the back of the Y-axis base, the gantry's side plate and the drag chain bracket
clamps: before cutting, check the trim router will not hit a clamp's long screw, and use the short one if it would
bit: unscrew the ER11 nut, put the bit in the collet, screw it back, tighten with two wrenches; the holes drilled in the nut are for balance
wiring: open the drag chain's links with a screwdriver, lay the spindle cable, the Z limit switch cable and the Z motor cable in it
connect each axis's motor and limit switch cable
connect the trim router's cable and tie it
bundle the trim router, limit switch and motor cables with zip ties and cable wrap
plug every cable into the controller and fit the antenna

faq.about: the PC does not see the serial port, or the machine will not move after power on
faq.answer: check the CH340 driver, check whether the emergency stop or a limit switch is triggered, try another USB socket

faq.about: the machine moves and the trimmer does not turn
faq.answer: check its cable, its own switch, and that the R/M switch on the control board is at R
clean the machine, repack it, write to support

check each axis's limit switch cable is in its own socket; check the emergency stop is released; a damaged switch, cable or driver, or changed configuration, is for support, with a video of the home. Alarm 8 in the console means a limit switch was already triggered when Home was pressed: release it first
